thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT OPENED — P1 — smart-routing fallback loop + dedicated pool blackhole. Detected 2026-10-12 03:12 UTC. Initial signal: dedicated-pool autoscaler observed sudden drop in 'active-instances' metric for pool-us-west-2, routed traffic to fallback variant 'gpt-small-quant' which had zero hot instances, resulting in requests queued/blackholed. Pager triggered. runbook: https://internal/runbooks/smart-routing-fallback

sanjay: seeing same. Grafana shows pool-us-west-2 active_instances -> 0 at 03:09, then router started routing to fallback variant 03:10. CPU on fallback variants is fine but connections are failing, cluster returns 503s.

ashley: tagging customer-impact: several customers on dedicated tier report increased latency and 5xxs. CX reported 2 major customers (acme-corp, pinefinance) hitting errors.

mike: quick triage — is this autoscaler misreading a metric, or upstream exporter flapping? I see kube-probe errors in dedicated pool nodes right before spike.

beatrice: checking metric path. It looks like our router maps KV cache-evictions metric to 'active-instances' in the scalarization step when backend returns no heartbeat. Suspect mapping bug in metric-translator v2.1.

ashley: customer impact status: acme-corp - 30% failed requests for last 6m, pinefinance - 15%. we should notify CS and set bridge.

incident-bot: bridge created: https://zoom/bridge/1234. PagerDuty escalation: oncall-sre -> sanjay.

sanjay: taking pager. immediate mitigation idea: 1) disable fallback routing policy to stop routing to variants with zero capacity; 2) scale up pool-us-west-2 manually; 3) force router to fallback to regional variant in eu-west-1 as temporary. Any objections?

mike: +1 to disable fallback policy. How to flip quickly?

beatrice: we can patch router policy via admin API:

```json
PATCH /admin/router/policies/active
{ "disable_fallback": true }
```

mike: running now (cli):
`redwoodctl router patch --disable-fallback --policy-id active`

ops-runbook-bot: Executed command by mike at 03:18 UTC: patch accepted, ttl=60s until autosync.

sanjay: monitor metric after patch. also starting manual scale: `redwoodctl pools scale --pool pool-us-west-2 --replicas 8`

ops-runbook-bot: scale command submitted, nodes provisioning expected ~2m.

eva: I'm looking at router logs: fallback selection was using variant-capacity metric from metric-translator v2.1 which returned 0 for quantized variants due to new tag name mismatch ("instance_count" vs "instances"). So the router thought those variants had zero capacity.

beatrice: yep that's the mapping bug i called out. patching metric-translator to read both keys as fallback: adding compatibility shim.

mike: scale finished, pool nodes come up, health checks passing.

incident-bot: metrics: pooled_active_instances for pool-us-west-2 now 8 at 03:22 UTC. 5xxs dropping.

ashley: contacting affected customers: acme-corp and pinefinance notified with ETA 10m and workaround (retry and region header). CS will follow up.

sanjay: router fallback disable worked — traffic no longer sent to zero-instance variants. But note: disabling fallback increases latency for some requests; communicate to product.

beatrice: deploy metric-translator patch to canary at 03:25, monitoring.

ops-runbook-bot: canary metrics OK for 5m, translator now returns integer instance counts for variants.

beatrice: promoting patch to prod.

mike: promo done at 03:31. router now sees correct capacity across variants. Re-enabling fallback with safer checks (min_instances:1) only after we confirm no zero mappings.

sanjay: re-enable fallback with new policy:

```json
PATCH /admin/router/policies/active
{ "disable_fallback": false, "fallback_min_instances": 1 }
```

mike: applied.

incident-bot: Observed behavior: 5xx rate returned to baseline at 03:34 UTC, customer errors resolving. Severity downgraded to P2 at 03:36 UTC.

ashley: postmortem actions to file: 1) add integration test for metric-translator key rename, 2) add router safety guard preventing fallback to variant with zero instances, 3) add alert if autoscaler sees sudden zero and fallback engaged, 4) update runbook with explicit manual-scale steps.

sanjay: assigning postmortem to beatrice, ETA 72h.

beatrice: ack. I'll include timeline, root cause (metric key rename in translator -> zero capacity), mitigations, and follow-ups.

eva: note for infra: autoscaler should prefer health checks over translated metric for immediate scale decisions. filing infra ticket.

mike: thumbs. Any remaining customer actions?

ashley: CS will send detailed incident note to acme-corp and pinefinance. internal RCA to be published when postmortem ready.

incident-bot: Incident closed to active mitigation at 03:45 UTC; follow-ups logged: CAL-432 (translator test), INF-987 (autoscaler health priority), RUNBOOK-21 (manual scale steps).

sanjay: handing off monitoring to oncall for next 2 hours. I'm offline after 04:00 UTC.

eva: I'll watch dashboards for next hour. ping me on slack if anything flares. :white_check_mark:

beatrice: will start postmortem doc now.

mike: great work team. quick debrief later. :coffee:
